title: India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
summary: The India-UAE CEPA is a landmark free trade agreement that provides duty-free access for 90% of Indian goods exported to UAE and grants Indian importers preferential access to over 99% of UAE products. Key sectors include gems and jewellery, textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, and electronics.

key_provisions.title: Tariff Elimination Schedule
key_provisions.content: Each Party shall eliminate or reduce its customs duties on originating goods of the other Party in accordance with its Tariff Elimination Schedule set out in Annex 2-A.

key_provisions.title: Rules of Origin
key_provisions.content: A good shall be treated as an originating good of a Party if it is wholly obtained or produced entirely in the territory of one or both Parties, or satisfies the requirements of Annex 3-A.

key_provisions.title: Cumulation
key_provisions.content: For the purposes of determining whether a good is originating, a producer of a good may have recourse to the originating materials of both Parties.

key_provisions.title: Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures
key_provisions.content: The Parties affirm their rights and obligations under the WTO Agreement on the Application of Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures.

title: Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership
summary: RCEP is the world's largest free trade agreement by GDP coverage, covering approximately 30% of global GDP. It includes ASEAN member states plus Australia, China, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea. The agreement covers trade in goods, services, investment, intellectual property, e-commerce, competition policy, and SMEs.

key_provisions.title: Trade in Goods
key_provisions.content: Parties shall progressively liberalise trade in goods over a transition period. The agreement provides for tariff reductions and elimination on over 90% of goods traded between member countries.

key_provisions.title: Rules of Origin
key_provisions.content: A product qualifies as originating if it has undergone sufficient production within RCEP member countries. The Regional Value Content (RVC) threshold is generally 40% or a Change in Tariff Classification (CTC) criterion.

key_provisions.title: Electronic Commerce
key_provisions.content: Parties shall maintain a legal framework governing electronic transactions consistent with the principles of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce.

title: EU-India Broad-Based Trade and Investment Agreement (Under Negotiation)
summary: The EU-India BTIA negotiations were relaunched in June 2022 after a decade-long pause. When concluded, it will be one of the most significant bilateral trade agreements between the EU and a major emerging economy. Key areas include goods, services, investment protection, government procurement, and sustainable development.

key_provisions.title: Market Access for Goods
key_provisions.content: Both parties aim for substantial liberalisation of tariffs with a target of 90%+ goods covered with preferential rates within 10 years of entry into force.
